keyVerseText: And Leah said, God hath given me my hire, because I have given my maiden to my husband: and she called his name Issachar. Issachar: that is, An hire
rootMeaning: The name יִשָּׂשכָר (Yissâˢkâr) derives from the Hebrew roots נָשָׂא (nâsâʼ) meaning 'to bear, bring, or carry' and שָׂכָר (sâkar) meaning 'reward' or 'hire.' Literally, it can be understood as 'he will bring a reward' or 'there is recompense.' This etymology highlights a sense of receiving or bringing forth a just payment or compensation, which adds depth beyond the simple English name 'Issachar' by emphasizing God's providential reward or blessing.
usageInScripture: The word יִשָּׂשכָר appears 43 times in Scripture, predominantly as a proper noun referring to the ninth son of Jacob and the tribe descending from him. Most translations (26 occurrences) render it as 'of Issachar,' indicating possession or lineage, while others simply use 'Issachar' as a name. This consistent use as a tribal and personal name underscores its importance in Israel's genealogical and territorial identity, with occasional references to the land allocated to the tribe, reflecting both people and place.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יִשָּׂשכָר as 'there is recompense' reminds believers that God is a just rewarder who honors faithfulness and obedience. As Issachar was a son of Jacob and progenitor of a tribe, his name embodies God's faithfulness in fulfilling promises and providing for His people. This meaning encourages trust in God's providential care and the assurance that labor and sacrifice in His service are not in vain. It also foreshadows the spiritual recompense believers receive through Christ, who perfectly embodies God's reward for righteousness.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 30:18 states, 'And Leah said, God hath given me my hire, because I have given my maiden to my husband: and she called his name Issachar. Issachar: that is, An hire.' Here, the name יִשָּׂשכָר explicitly connects to the concept of recompense or reward, as Leah acknowledges God's blessing as a just payment for her faithfulness. The word's meaning enriches this verse by highlighting God's role as the one who recompenses, affirming that human efforts in obedience are met with divine blessing.
